title: contourSlice rings have visible angles; rounding must be on by default
notes: Root cause: scene3d.js buildSliceSegments emits triangle-cut crossing points verbatim, so a pole-adjacent ring on a sphere/torus (few, long, oblique mesh edges) has as few as 4-31 vertices with up to 58.14 degree exterior turns (measured on r20/detail16/sliceCount26). Engine._applySceneCurveFinish cannot fully rescue this: reduceAnchors correctly marks the genuinely sharp turns corner:true and leaves them unrounded (2 hard corners survived on the worst pole ring pre-fix), which is the visible angle the user reported. Fix: Scene3D.Slices.refineRing (new) refines each LINKED ring in WORLD SPACE, before projection, with a centripetal Catmull-Rom (Barry-Goldman) interpolatory subdivision -- chosen over Chaikin corner-cutting because it INTERPOLATES every original vertex (Chaikin would shrink an already-inside-the-surface chord approximation further inside, failing the accuracy requirement). Refinement is adaptive: it re-measures the ring's max exterior turning angle and subdivides again only while it exceeds 12 degrees (capped at 6 rounds), so an already-smooth equatorial ring costs nothing extra. Gated on a NEW, independent smoothness predicate (SLICE_SMOOTH_EXCLUDED = box/plane/solid/pyramid), deliberately NOT Params.CURVED_FILL_PRIMITIVES, so this pass never couples to the surface-fill routing set. On the r20/detail16/sliceCount26 rig the worst ring's max turn dropped from 58.14deg to <=11.58deg across the whole sweep, its raw-vs-analytic-circle max radial deviation improved (1.0683mm -> 1.0673mm, i.e. MORE accurate, not just smoother), and its hard-corner count went from 2 to 0. A box's rectangular cross-section keeps its real ~90deg corners (never refined) -- confirmed both numerically and by byte-identical before/after screenshots for box and solid. Visually: the sphere/torus Tier-A contourSlice screenshots' innermost (pole-adjacent) ring changes from a visible 7-8 sided polygon to a materially rounder shape; box/solid screenshots are byte-identical (md5 match).
